title: Opening, Closing, Sitting Down, Standing Up
label: ch:spanish-open-close-sit-stand
canDo: I can say I open, close, sit down and stand up in Spanish, and use the reflexive pronoun that makes sentarse and levantarse land the action back on me.

payoff.summary: Say the chapter in one breath — abro el libro, me siento, cierro el libro, me levanto — then separate the two features it taught: sentarse is reflexive and a stem-changer, levantarse is reflexive only. Name the shared recipe behind both body-position verbs (a Latin present participle, sedēns and levāns), pick abierto out as the one irregular participle, and reach back to la mano for why the article stays feminine.
